correctness.rationale: The explicit parity law survives unchanged. The frozen limitation that finite-β equilibria retain disagreement is false without qualification. On a single edge with K=1, a=2/5, b=3/5, and innate vector (0,1), both rows of Ψ₁ are (3/5,2/5). The unique finite-β equilibrium is (2/5,2/5) for every 0≤β<1. The replacement proves the exact criterion: because Ψ_K is stochastic, a constant vector solves the fixed-point equation exactly when Ψ_K x* is constant, and uniqueness then applies. I checked the core proof for all positive K: each response is stochastic from the anchored update and is primitive since the graph edges and diagonal are positive (B+Z for K=1, and B and ZB among terms for K≥2). Reciprocity gives q_LW=q_R and q_RW=q_L, so on the left class rows Z is H and B is J. Since H²=abI, T_(2q) is a positive mixing of T_∞ and I; its two off-diagonals have fixed ratio. For K=2q+1 multiplying H by I−T_∞ adds the stated positive terms ab(1−a) and ab(1−b), each times (ab)^q/(1−ab). The stationary left mass is T₂₁/(T₁₂+T₂₁) and yields the asserted weights. The sign follows from a(1−b)²−b(1−a)²=(a−b)(1−ab). The repair states the exact sign for the selected value after multiplying by the initial mean difference; the odd deviation is Θ((ab)^q) for unequal susceptibilities and means, with asymptotic, not finite-step exact, ratio ab. The primitive stationary row preserves the mean at all β<1, and power convergence and its Abel limit give respectively the β=1 initialized result and β↑1 limit. On a weighted star the part means are the hub opinion and the degree-weighted leaf opinion; the given all-zero leaves make degree weighting immaterial. All four fractions check exactly.

reproduction.result: 72 exact full-matrix and finite-β invariant cases on three weighted graph shapes with three susceptibility pairs and K=1,…,8; 18 exact signed odd-even identities; star fractions 4/5, 16/17, 32/35, 16/17. The repair also corrects the star explanation: each part's degree total is the sum of the edge weights, equal to the number of leaves only in the unit-weight convention. The rank-one finite-β counterexample replays directly from its two rows; no solver is needed. The frozen verifier was inspected, not run. Bounded rational comparisons are not proofs for arbitrary K or graph size.

value.rationale: The peer horizon is a natural parameter in the specified feedback model. Its parity changes the selected value even though all transitions average: every even horizon has the same selected weight across all reciprocal bipartite graphs, while odd horizons deviate with a sharp sign and convergence law. The star shows that the effect does not vanish with community-size imbalance. This is an interpretable finite-horizon invariant, not merely a two-vertex counterexample or an empirical prediction. The correction to the finite-β limitation preserves this contribution.
